newsitem.title: MALTA: Voting starts in Malta's election "on Europe".
newsitem.headline: Voting starts in Malta's election "on Europe".

text.p: Maltese started voting on Saturday in a general election widely seen as a referendum on whether the island should pursue its bid to enter the European Union.

Two main parties are vying for the votes of the 275,000 electorate, with the ruling Nationalist Party promising to give priority to getting Malta into the EU while the Labour Party says it will drop the island's application.
Polling stations, set to open at 7 a.m., opened their doors a little later, apparently because of last-minute hitches with ballot boxes.
The Nationalist Party, led by Prime Minister Edward Fenech Adami, had a three seat majority over Alfred Sant's Labour Party in the 65-seat parliament.

The some 500 polling stations on Malta and the sister island of Gozo were due to close at 10 p.m. Malta's system of proportional representation means results are not expected until late on Sunday or early on Monday.
